spike_candidates.statement: Nathan's July 4 hot dog contest 'since 1916' was invented: promoter Mortimer Matz admitted in 2010 he made it up in the early 1970s.
spike_candidates.tension: The company's own history page still prints the 1916 contest as 'legend has it' while its first recorded contest is 1972 and the first official one was 1967.

spike_candidates.statement: A $30,000 film shot on Coney Island in 1953, Little Fugitive, made a 7-year-old with $6 the template for the French New Wave, per Truffaut.
spike_candidates.tension: The Coney Island it records, safe enough for a child alone, is the one the 1979 Warriors shows as shuttered and gone to seed.

spike_candidates.statement: Ruby's, open since 1934, was ordered out in November 2010 after the city paid $100 million for the amusement zone.
spike_candidates.tension: The street beside the bar is co-named for its owner, yet the city's own land deal started the eviction; no source here says whether the bar reopened.

spike_candidates.statement: The Warriors, the most famous Coney Island film, never filmed in the Bronx, and commenters say its beach ending was shot at Breezy Point or Fort Tilden.
spike_candidates.tension: The 'Coney Island' ending that fans quote may not be Coney Island, and the best proof is a reader comment, not an official source.

conflicts: Hot dog contest origin: legend 1916 (C060, Nathan's franchise page, 'legend has it') vs admitted fabrication by promoter Matz in 2010 (C058, C059, Wikipedia) vs first official contest June 30, 1967 (C057) vs first major recorded contest 1972 (C061). Most reliable: Wikipedia's account citing NYT reporting on Matz; Nathan's own 1972 date is consistent with 'early 1970s' fabrication. The 1916 contest is contradicted.
Nathan's 1916 start-up money: $300 life savings (C073, Wikipedia) vs $300 loan (C083, company page). Company page is the primary source, but Wikipedia cites NYT/UPI 1974; unresolved, say '$300'.

Second Nathan's location in Oceanside, Long Island: 1955 (company, in fact list) vs 1959 (Wikipedia, 'a second branch on long beach road in oceanside, new york, opened in 1959'). Company page is more authoritative on its own history but Wikipedia cites press; flag as unresolved.

Lou Reed's Coney Island Baby: released December 1975 (album page, the Wikipedia album article) vs 1976 (C010, popular culture hub; charts are 1976). Album page is more authoritative; use 'December 1975, charted 1976'.

Polar Bear plunge numbering: MCNY calls Jan 1, 2019 the 115th (C053) and 6sqft calls Jan 1, 2022 the 119th (C054). Counting from 1903 neither fits (2019 would be ~117th, 2022 ~120th) and 2021 was skipped; avoid ordinals or say 'since 1903'.

Mermaid Parade size: 3,000 participants and 'hundreds of thousands' of spectators (C097, Wikipedia text, 2024 6sqft) vs 5,000 participants (C104, 6sqft 2026) vs infobox attendance 30,000 (C098). Use ranges and attribute.

Ruby's eviction: landlord Central Amusement International (C122, Brooklyn Paper) vs Thor Equities (C128, Village Voice 'apparently'). Brooklyn Paper has the named landlord and lease detail; the city bought the land from Joe Sitt of Thor (C123). Prefer Brooklyn Paper.

Totonno's reopening after Sandy: five months closed (own site, C090 timeline entry for 2012-13) vs mid-January 2013 (C094, Wikipedia), which is about 2.5 months. Own site is internally inconsistent; unresolved.
Lombardi's date vs Pero's arrival: Wikipedia says Lombardi's was established in 1905 (C095) while Totonno's own timeline says Pero began working there in 1903. Unresolved; avoid stating both.

The Warriors ending: Brooklyn Magazine says the film ends under the Coney Island Wonder Wheel (C031), but reader comments on Scouting NY say the beach scene was Breezy Point/Fort Tilden (C032, C033). Comments are not authoritative; unresolved.
Hot dog record: Wikipedia main text says 74 (2018) in the Nathan's page vs 76 (2021, contest page, C068); the contest page is later and the more specific source.

Luna Park age: 6sqft says '120-year history' (C148) but the modern Luna Park opened in 2010 and the original ran 1903-44; the number counts the brand. Wikipedia list shows Luna Park (1903-44) as a separate former park.
dead_ends: Whether Ruby's Bar & Grill is open today and under what ownership; the only post-2010 hint is an undated oral-history line about the renovated Ruby's (C129).
Whether Totonno's was sold after the May 2024 call for a buyer, its current hours, prices and wait times.
Gargiulo's (1907 founding claim), Williams Candy, Coney Island Brewery and other named restaurants: no harvested page.
Current menu prices at Nathan's, hours, and whether the Smithfield deal closed.

Weegee's 1940 beach photo at the V&A and the Macaulay 'Little Odessa by the Sea' essay were in the URL list but not in the bundle; no Diane Arbus, Reginald Marsh or Joseph Stella detail beyond the Time Out listing.
Who visits the beach today (demographics, languages, crowds); any 2025-26 reporting on beach culture itself, such as volleyball, fishing, Sunday gatherings, vendor rules.
Mermaid Parade 2026 actual turnout and route details; Polar Bear Club recent plunge counts and current numbering.
Dates of the Brighton Jubilee festival, Coney Island Film Festival and other recurring local events.
Primary-source proof of the Warriors' final beach location (only reader comments).

recency.newest_item: Wikipedia pages dated Aug 2026 report Nathan's sale to Smithfield (announced 2026-01-21, $450M), Joey Chestnut's 66 hot dogs at the 2026 contest, and the 44th Mermaid Parade on 2026-06-20 funded by a GoFundMe ($42,000+) and a $20,000 pledge from the Borough President. Ruby's and Totonno's items are older (2010; May 2024).
